chunks: The Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from Aḥmad ibn Idrīs, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Faḍālah ibn Ayyūb, from al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿUthmān, from Samāʿah, from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
If you have performed part of your wudu (ablution), then some need arises for you such that your wudu dries, then repeat your wudu, for wudu does not admit division.
And by this isnad, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār, who said:

I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: Sometimes I perform wudu (ablution), then the water runs out, so I call the servant-girl, but she delays bringing me the water, and my wudu dries. He said: Repeat it.
As for what Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā narrated from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Mughīrah, from Ḥarīz:

Concerning wudu (ablution) drying, he said: I said: What if the first part dries before I wash the part that follows it? He said: Whether it has dried or not, wash what remains. I said: And likewise ghusl due to janabah? He said: It is at that same level; begin with the head, then pour over the rest of your body. I said: Even if it is after part of a day? He said: Yes.

Thus, the proper understanding of this report is that if the one performing wudu (ablution) did not interrupt his wudu, but rather a strong wind or intense heat dried it, then in that case repetition is not obligatory upon him. Repetition is only obligatory when the wudu is deliberately separated while the time and air are moderate. It is also possible that it came by way of taqiyyah, because that is the doctrine of many of the ʿammah.

key_terms.أَعِدْ: repeat it; restart the act from the beginning
key_terms.التَّقِيَّةِ: dissimulation for protection; issuing a ruling in conformity with others under certain circumstances
key_terms.تَفْرِيقِ الْوُضُوءِ: separating the acts of wudu with interruption
key_terms.غُسْلُ الْجَنَابَةِ: the ritual bath due to janabah
key_terms.وُضُوءُكَ: your wudu (ablution), the ritual washing being discussed
key_terms.يَتَبَعَّضُ: to be divided into separated parts; here, lacking continuity

ai.seo_question: If the limbs of wudu dry before finishing, must the wudu be repeated?
ai.summary: This report discusses the ruling of continuity in wudu (ablution) and whether drying between its parts requires repetition. It presents reports commanding repetition when wudu is interrupted, then reconciles another report by distinguishing accidental drying from intentional separation, while also noting the possibility of taqiyyah.
